nodes.name: Shutters Yawn
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Swap day begins before the shutters finish yawning, and the best tables hide in back.{pause}If the last blue spine is here, it will be under cables, not posing beside the glass.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}The bright swap-day tune returns to its opening four notes, turning caution into a pleasant{pause}rhythm.{pause}They have learned that a complete shelf means little if completing it makes the afternoon{pause}smaller.

nodes.name: The Empty Slot
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: I brought the shelf card so we remember the exact gap instead of buying another almost-match.{pause}That empty space has followed us through six markets and one famously terrible online auction.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}Aya checks the list again, not because she forgot, but because anticipation enjoys a tiny ceremony.{pause}Every clue deserves time to be wrong before either of them turns it into a convenient legend.

nodes.name: Why Blue
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: You started this row because the first cart arrived with your grandmother's train{pause}tickets inside.{pause}Completing it is not a contest; it is a way of giving those tickets a neighborhood.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}Ren leaves both hands visible near the table; good trades begin before anyone names a price.{pause}The blue row matters because people carried it here, one bus ride and careful sleeve at a time.

nodes.name: Low Tables
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The expensive stalls display perfect boxes, but the low table has manuals softened by actual hands.{pause}I would rather meet a worn game with a history than a flawless object with a guard.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}Around them, collectors compare scratches, stories, and impossible memories of old bargains.{pause}Neither collector wants perfection badly enough to erase the hands that kept the game alive.

nodes.name: Three Candidates
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Faded loose cart, near-mint box, and manual pouch with one blue corner showing.{pause}All three could fill the slot, but only one may carry the story we came to honor.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}A case snaps shut nearby, crisp as punctuation at the end of somebody else's successful hunt.{pause}The next decision will change the cart's future, so they practice saying their reasons aloud.

nodes.name: Pencil Boss
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The pouch contains boss tips in careful pencil and a note saying trade fairly at the station.{pause}Whoever wrote this expected the manual to travel farther than the person who owned it.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}The bright swap-day tune returns to its opening four notes, turning caution into a pleasant{pause}rhythm.{pause}For a moment, the hunt becomes quiet enough for friendship to show through the price talk.

nodes.name: First Test
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Before we decide what looks rare, we decide what evidence deserves our first attention.{pause}A shell, a box, and a manual can each tell the truth from a different direction.{pause}The test counter smells of warm batteries while its old mono screen waits for a small miracle.{pause}Aya checks the list again, not because she forgot, but because anticipation enjoys a tiny ceremony.{pause}A tiny title can hold a long journey when somebody bothers to remember where it traveled.

nodes.name: Aya's Rule
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: Let us choose one lead and follow it properly instead of sampling every rumor until it agrees.{pause}The first check will shape the offer we make when the station trader finally arrives.{pause}The test counter smells of warm batteries while its old mono screen waits for a small miracle.{pause}Ren leaves both hands visible near the table; good trades begin before anyone names a price.{pause}They have learned that a complete shelf means little if completing it makes the afternoon{pause}smaller.

nodes.name: Honest Wear
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The faded loose cart carries the crescent mark and wear from hundreds of careful insertions.{pause}Choosing use over shine helps Mrs. Imai trust that we understand the traveling route.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}Around them, collectors compare scratches, stories, and impossible memories of old bargains.{pause}Every clue deserves time to be wrong before either of them turns it into a convenient legend.

nodes.name: Perfect Decoy
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: The near-mint box contains a donation note pointing us back toward the played loose copy.{pause}Choosing condition first teaches us that perfection can be evidence without being the destination.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}A case snaps shut nearby, crisp as punctuation at the end of somebody else's successful hunt.{pause}The blue row matters because people carried it here, one bus ride and careful sleeve at a time.

nodes.name: Paper Route
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The manual pouch reveals the station times, pencil bosses, and the crescent ownership mark.{pause}Choosing paper first lets the former keepers speak before the hardware gives us its answer.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}The bright swap-day tune returns to its opening four notes, turning caution into a pleasant{pause}rhythm.{pause}Neither collector wants perfection badly enough to erase the hands that kept the game alive.

nodes.name: Clean Board
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Whichever lead we followed, the board is clean and the battery tab was replaced carefully.{pause}A tiny mark near the contacts matches the crescent drawn beside the manual's station note.{pause}The test counter smells of warm batteries while its old mono screen waits for a small miracle.{pause}Aya checks the list again, not because she forgot, but because anticipation enjoys a tiny ceremony.{pause}The next decision will change the cart's future, so they practice saying their reasons aloud.

nodes.name: Next Owner
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The cart boots to one save named NEXT OWNER and a star map missing its final point.{pause}That is either wonderfully polite game design or a message hidden by a patient collector.{pause}The test counter smells of warm batteries while its old mono screen waits for a small miracle.{pause}Ren leaves both hands visible near the table; good trades begin before anyone names a price.{pause}For a moment, the hunt becomes quiet enough for friendship to show through the price talk.

nodes.name: Three Stations
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: The star map matches three stations, each with a time scribbled inside the manual cover.{pause}Our seller says an older woman tested the cart here every summer and never sold it.{pause}The test counter smells of warm batteries while its old mono screen waits for a small miracle.{pause}Around them, collectors compare scratches, stories, and impossible memories of old bargains.{pause}A tiny title can hold a long journey when somebody bothers to remember where it traveled.

nodes.name: The Summer Table
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: She lent it to new collectors, then asked them to leave one note before returning it.{pause}The worn label is not neglect; it is the visible mileage of a small traveling library.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}A case snaps shut nearby, crisp as punctuation at the end of somebody else's successful hunt.{pause}They have learned that a complete shelf means little if completing it makes the afternoon{pause}smaller.

nodes.name: A Near-Mint Decoy
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: The perfect boxed copy belongs to the same title, donated only to fund today's swap room.{pause}Its owner wants the played cart to find someone who understands why it stayed loose.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}The bright swap-day tune returns to its opening four notes, turning caution into a pleasant{pause}rhythm.{pause}Every clue deserves time to be wrong before either of them turns it into a convenient legend.

nodes.name: Lunch Money
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The asking price is fair, but paying cash would leave a younger buyer short on batteries.{pause}I can trade my duplicate puzzle cart instead, if we stop treating duplicates as security blankets.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}Aya checks the list again, not because she forgot, but because anticipation enjoys a tiny ceremony.{pause}The blue row matters because people carried it here, one bus ride and careful sleeve at a time.

nodes.name: Platform Two
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: The manual's final note points to platform two, where the former keeper waits beside a thermos.{pause}She recognizes the crescent immediately and asks what we noticed before asking what we{pause}offer.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}Ren leaves both hands visible near the table; good trades begin before anyone names a price.{pause}Neither collector wants perfection badly enough to erase the hands that kept the game alive.

nodes.name: Mrs. Imai
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: Mrs. Imai says the next owner must add a star without erasing any previous route.{pause}She cares less about our shelf than whether we can make room for someone after us.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}Around them, collectors compare scratches, stories, and impossible memories of old bargains.{pause}The next decision will change the cart's future, so they practice saying their reasons aloud.

nodes.name: Her First WonderSwan
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: She bought the cart after missing her train and played until the next service arrived.{pause}Every later note came from another stranded traveler invited to borrow the little blue world.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}A case snaps shut nearby, crisp as punctuation at the end of somebody else's successful hunt.{pause}For a moment, the hunt becomes quiet enough for friendship to show through the price talk.

nodes.name: The Final Point
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The missing star belongs to this station today; the save has been waiting for our decision.{pause}Booting, reading, or trading can each honor the route, but none leaves it unchanged.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}The bright swap-day tune returns to its opening four notes, turning caution into a pleasant{pause}rhythm.{pause}A tiny title can hold a long journey when somebody bothers to remember where it traveled.

nodes.name: Gentle Terms
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Mrs. Imai asks for no premium, only a fair exchange and a written promise to share.{pause}The hunt suddenly feels less like victory than being handed a warm cup on a platform.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}Aya checks the list again, not because she forgot, but because anticipation enjoys a tiny ceremony.{pause}They have learned that a complete shelf means little if completing it makes the afternoon{pause}smaller.

nodes.name: The Blue Sentence
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: At home, the shelf row finally forms its tiny blue sentence beneath grandmother's tickets.{pause}The last word does not look like an ending; it looks like a place to begin reading.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}Ren leaves both hands visible near the table; good trades begin before anyone names a price.{pause}Every clue deserves time to be wrong before either of them turns it into a convenient legend.

nodes.name: Fresh Sleeve
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: We fit a soft sleeve without cleaning away the crescent or the honest wear around it.{pause}Preservation means protecting use, not polishing every object until nobody appears to{pause}have lived.{pause}The market shelves rise around them, crowded with blue spines, handwritten prices, and soft dust.{pause}Around them, collectors compare scratches, stories, and impossible memories of old bargains.{pause}The blue row matters because people carried it here, one bus ride and careful sleeve at a time.

nodes.name: One More Rule
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The star map waits on the test screen while I decide what promise enters the shelf card.{pause}This last move will say whether the collection keeps, remembers, or circulates its luck.{pause}The test counter smells of warm batteries while its old mono screen waits for a small miracle.{pause}A case snaps shut nearby, crisp as punctuation at the end of somebody else's successful hunt.{pause}Neither collector wants perfection badly enough to erase the hands that kept the game alive.

nodes.name: Mint Green
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: I boot the cart with Mrs. Imai present, and the final star blooms mint green.{pause}Our first choice supplied the clue; this choice turns it into a shared, audible moment.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}The bright swap-day tune returns to its opening four notes, turning caution into a pleasant{pause}rhythm.{pause}The next decision will change the cart's future, so they practice saying their reasons aloud.

nodes.name: All the Notes
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: We read every save note aloud before adding the station date and Aya's promise.{pause}The shelf receives not only a cart, but the full chain of people who carried it.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}Aya checks the list again, not because she forgot, but because anticipation enjoys a tiny ceremony.{pause}For a moment, the hunt becomes quiet enough for friendship to show through the price talk.

nodes.name: Fair Exchange
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: I trade the duplicate puzzle cart, keeping lunch money and sending another game outward.{pause}The blue spine comes home because the collection learned how to release something first.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}Ren leaves both hands visible near the table; good trades begin before anyone names a price.{pause}A tiny title can hold a long journey when somebody bothers to remember where it traveled.

nodes.name: Good End: Blue Chime
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: The title chime answers from the completed row, bright enough to reach the next room.{pause}A shelf that can still be played never has to mistake completion for silence.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}Around them, collectors compare scratches, stories, and impossible memories of old bargains.{pause}They have learned that a complete shelf means little if completing it makes the afternoon{pause}smaller.

nodes.name: Good End: Next Owner
nodes.speaker: Aya
nodes.dialogue: The last note says found at summer swap, kept with care, ready for another traveler.{pause}My blue sentence ends with a comma, exactly where Mrs. Imai hoped it would.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}A case snaps shut nearby, crisp as punctuation at the end of somebody else's successful hunt.{pause}Every clue deserves time to be wrong before either of them turns it into a convenient legend.

nodes.name: Good End: Fair Shelf
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: The duplicate finds a delighted owner before our train arrives, balancing the whole afternoon.{pause}Aya fills the final slot without making the world outside her shelf any poorer.{pause}Afternoon light crosses the station table, and each arriving train rattles the loose plastic{pause}cases.{pause}The bright swap-day tune returns to its opening four notes, turning caution into a pleasant{pause}rhythm.{pause}The blue row matters because people carried it here, one bus ride and careful sleeve at a time.
